science.label: Field science
science.blurb: Geological process fidelity first: rocks, dryness, surface.

environment.label: Hardware & environment
environment.blurb: Thermal, atmospheric and moisture stress on equipment and crews.

mobility.label: Rover mobility
mobility.blurb: Slopes, relief and roughness at traverse-planning scale.

ice.label: Ice prospecting
ice.blurb: Frozen ground, cold and dryness for volatile-access rehearsal.

datasets.name: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model (ice surface)
datasets.measures: Surface elevation (topography over land; bathymetry masked out here).
datasets.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, 2022. doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74
datasets.used_for: Terrain: slope distribution, relief, roughness scaling
datasets.limits: Blend of Copernicus DEM, ICESat-2-corrected sources and polar DEMs; vertical accuracy varies by source. Slopes here are km-scale and say nothing about metre-scale hazards.

datasets.name: MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR)
datasets.measures: Mars topography from laser altimetry, referenced to the areoid.
datasets.citation: Smith et al. 2001, J. Geophys. Res. 106, 23689; Smith et al. 2003, MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0, NASA PDS
datasets.limits: Along-track shot spacing 300 m but cross-track gaps of 1–4 km near the equator; the 32 px/deg grid was chosen because most of its cells contain real shots.

datasets.name: LRO LOLA Gridded Data Record (LDEM_16)
datasets.measures: Lunar topography from laser altimetry, relative to a 1737.4 km sphere.
datasets.citation: Smith et al. 2010, Space Sci. Rev. 150, 209; LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, NASA PDS
datasets.limits: Resampled far below LOLA's native density so that ground sampling matches the Earth and Mars grids.

datasets.name: LRO Diviner Global Cumulative Products (GCP)
datasets.measures: Bolometric brightness temperature of the lunar surface vs local time.
datasets.format: PDS3 fixed-width ASCII table (read by HTTP range request)
datasets.used_for: Moon reference temperatures (mean, day–night range, night mean)
datasets.limits: A 0.5° bin spans ~15 km: at the poles it mixes sunlit and permanently shadowed ground.

datasets.name: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Products (PRP)
datasets.measures: Annual average and maximum surface temperature; modelled depth to stable water ice.
datasets.format: PDS3 fixed-width ASCII table (read by HTTP range request)
datasets.used_for: Polar reference temperatures; cold-trap fraction (Tmax < 110 K)
datasets.limits: Ice-stability depth is a thermal-model product, not a detection of ice.

datasets.name: Mars Climate Database v6.2
datasets.agency: LMD / Open University / IAA / ESA / CNES
datasets.measures: Climatological surface temperature, surface pressure and dust column optical depth from a general circulation model validated against orbital and landed data.
datasets.citation: Millour et al. 2022, The Mars Climate Database (version 6), EPSC2022-786; Forget et al. 1999, J. Geophys. Res. 104, 24155
datasets.used_for: Mars reference temperatures (annual mean, diurnal range, coldest season), pressure, dust
datasets.limits: MODEL OUTPUT, not measurement. Used because no single instrument record is diurnally and seasonally complete at every site. Graded lower in the confidence score.

datasets.name: MGS TES Bolometric Albedo Global Mosaic
datasets.measures: Solar-band (0.3–2.9 µm) Lambert albedo of the Martian surface.
datasets.citation: Christensen et al. 2001, J. Geophys. Res. 106, 23823
datasets.limits: Dust redistribution changes regional albedo by a few hundredths between Mars years.

datasets.name: MODIS/Terra Land Surface Temperature, monthly CMG (MOD11C3)
datasets.agency: NASA LP DAAC, served by NASA GIBS
datasets.measures: Clear-sky radiometric skin temperature at ~10:30 and ~22:30 local time.
datasets.resolution: 0.05° product, sampled at 0.1°; 0.6 K value bins (GIBS palette)
datasets.format: Palette PNG decoded with the official GIBS colormap
datasets.citation: Wan, Hook & Hulley 2021, MOD11C3 v061, NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD11C3.061
datasets.used_for: Mean annual surface temperature, coldest month, frozen fraction
datasets.limits: Clear-sky only; values below 200 K are clipped by the palette; two overpasses under-sample the diurnal cycle (so diurnal range comes from MERRA-2).

datasets.name: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Index, monthly (MOD13)
datasets.agency: NASA LP DAAC, served by NASA GIBS
datasets.format: Palette PNG decoded with the official GIBS colormap
datasets.citation: Didan 2021, MOD13A3 v061, NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13A3.061
datasets.limits: Single year; snow depresses NDVI at high latitudes.

datasets.name: MODIS Combined BRDF/Albedo, black-sky shortwave (MCD43)
datasets.agency: NASA LP DAAC, served by NASA GIBS
datasets.temporal: Seven seasonal dates 2021–2023; lower quartile used to suppress snow
datasets.format: Palette PNG decoded with the official GIBS colormap
datasets.citation: Schaaf & Wang 2021, MCD43A3 v061, NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MCD43A3.061
datasets.limits: Not identical to the TES 0.3–2.9 µm band; seven dates are a sparse sample. CERES SYN1deg fills cells with no retrieval.

datasets.name: MODIS Land Cover Type, IGBP classes (MCD12)
datasets.agency: NASA LP DAAC, served by NASA GIBS
datasets.measures: Annual land-cover class (water, barren, snow/ice, vegetation types).
datasets.format: Palette PNG decoded with the official GIBS colormap
datasets.citation: Friedl & Sulla-Menashe 2022, MCD12Q1 v061, NASA LP DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MCD12Q1.061
datasets.used_for: Land / water mask for terrain windows; barren and ice fractions (context only)
datasets.limits: Where unmapped, land is taken as ETOPO elevation above sea level.

datasets.name: MERRA-2 reanalysis climatology via NASA POWER
datasets.measures: Skin temperature and its hourly range, column water vapour, surface pressure, wind, corrected precipitation.
datasets.citation: Gelaro et al. 2017, J. Climate 30, 5419; NASA POWER Project, NASA Langley Research Center
datasets.used_for: Diurnal temperature range, column water vapour, surface pressure; fallback temperature and precipitation
datasets.limits: Reanalysis (model constrained by observations). ~55 km cells cannot resolve valley-scale microclimates such as individual Dry Valleys.

datasets.name: GPM IMERG precipitation climatology via NASA POWER
datasets.coverage: Global (reduced skill over snow/ice and at high latitude)
datasets.citation: Huffman et al. 2023, GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 V07, NASA GES DISC. doi:10.5067/GPM/IMERG/3B-MONTH/07
datasets.limits: Known to over-estimate in hyper-arid cores (a few mm/yr of spurious light rain). Scores therefore saturate at 1 mm/yr.

datasets.name: CERES SYN1deg surface albedo and aerosol optical depth via NASA POWER
datasets.measures: Clear-sky surface albedo; aerosol optical depth at 0.55 µm (MODIS-constrained).
datasets.citation: Doelling et al. 2013, J. Atmos. Oceanic Technol. 30, 1072; Rutan et al. 2015, J. Atmos. Oceanic Technol. 32, 1121
datasets.limits: 1° cells (~110 km). AOD includes smoke and pollution as well as mineral dust.

datasets.name: Macrostrat global geologic map compilation
datasets.measures: Mapped bedrock / surficial units with lithology and age at a point.
datasets.citation: Peters, Husson & Czaplewski 2018, Geochem. Geophys. Geosyst. 19, 1393 (CC-BY 4.0)
datasets.used_for: Site-tier lithology classes (independent of the gridded scan)
datasets.limits: Coarse units; lithology strings classified by keyword. Impact structures, lava tubes and periglacial landforms are not encoded.

datasets.name: Natural Earth physical regions and administrative units
datasets.limits: Names are labels, not analysis inputs.

datasets.name: Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic & NASA Blue Marble
datasets.agency: ESA Copernicus (EOX IT Services) / NASA GIBS
datasets.citation: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2020 by EOX IT Services GmbH (contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2020); NASA Blue Marble Next Generation
datasets.limits: Display only — imagery is never an input to the scores.

limitations.title: Earth cannot reproduce gravity
limitations.body: Lunar gravity is 0.17 g and Martian gravity 0.38 g. Regolith flow, dust lofting, vehicle traction and human locomotion all depend on it. No field site changes this.

limitations.title: No vacuum, no thin CO₂ atmosphere
limitations.body: The Moon has no atmosphere and Mars averages ~0.6 kPa. The highest ice-free ground on Earth is still above 45 kPa. Our pressure score therefore stays low everywhere, by design.

limitations.title: Radiation environment
limitations.body: Galactic cosmic rays, solar particle events and unfiltered ultraviolet reach the lunar and Martian surface. Earth's magnetosphere and ozone layer shield every analog site.

limitations.title: Temperatures only approach, never match
limitations.body: Lunar permanently shadowed regions sit near 40–100 K and the equatorial lunar day swings by about 290 K. Mars swings 60–90 K daily around ~210 K. Earth's coldest ice-free ground closes only part of that gap; the app reports exactly how much.

limitations.title: Different geological histories
limitations.body: Earth has plate tectonics, liquid water and life. Lunar regolith was made by billions of years of impacts in vacuum; Martian soils carry perchlorates and nanophase iron oxides. Matching rock type is not matching material.

limitations.title: Scale of the terrain comparison
limitations.body: Slopes and roughness are compared at a 1.9–15 km baseline because that is the scale at which all three global elevation models are comparable. Rock abundance and metre-scale hazards are not assessed.

limitations.title: Resolution and time mismatch
limitations.body: Inputs range from 0.5 km to 110 km and from single years to multi-decade climatologies. Valley-scale microclimates (for example individual Antarctic Dry Valleys) are partly averaged with their surroundings.

limitations.title: Models and proxies are labelled
limitations.body: Mars climate comes from a general circulation model; Earth's diurnal range, humidity and pressure from a reanalysis; ground ice is inferred from temperature. These are graded lower than direct measurements in the confidence score.

limitations.title: Selection effects in validation
limitations.body: Established analog sites were chosen partly for road access, existing stations and funding geography, not purely for physical similarity. A physical-similarity method should recover the environmentally-motivated sites and is not expected to recover sites chosen for geochemistry or logistics.

limitations.title: A candidate is a hypothesis
limitations.body: A high score says the measured variables resemble the reference region. It is an argument for a field visit, not a substitute for one.

sensitivity.description: Each run redraws factor weights (log-normal, σ=0.5), the tolerance multiplier (0.25–1.0), the precipitation floor (2–20 mm/yr), the aggregator (geometric 70% / arithmetic 30%) and drops one factor 25% of the time.
